01-modes.title: Modes: Design · Code · Concept · Debug
01-modes.why: Pick how Beast should answer. Concept has Full and ⚡ Short (a 3-line definition, fastest).
steps: Choose Concept (Full): type a question, press Enter
Full answer: concept · use case · diagram · example
Switch to ⚡ Short and ask the same
Short: just the definition, ≤3 lines

02-screenshot-send.title: Screenshot & send: 💻 or ⌘↵
02-screenshot-send.why: One click (or ⌘↵) grabs the whole screen and sends it with anything you typed. The answer opens at once.
steps: The question is on the screen (LeetCode)
Code mode · type “in Python” · click 💻
Sent screenshot shows next to “Asked:”
Answer: approach · dry run · code · complexity
Empty bar + ⌘↵ works the same

03-area-screenshot.title: Area screenshot: ⌘⇧S
03-area-screenshot.why: Drag over just the part you want. It waits in the tray so you can add a note or more screenshots, then Enter sends.
steps: Press ⌘⇧S: the screen dims
Drag a box around the problem
The crop waits in the tray (nothing sent yet)
✎ Add a note for this screenshot
Press Enter: answer follows the note

04-followups.title: Follow-ups: more text, screenshots and files in the same conversation
04-followups.why: Every answer has a follow-up box. Add a screenshot, an area or a file, type a question, and it continues the same thread.
steps: Ask with 💻 (Code · LeetCode on screen)
The screen changes: buggy code
Follow-up box: + Screen and type the question
Send: Q1 stays above with its screenshot
📎 attach a log file + ask again
+ New starts a fresh conversation

05-history-continue.title: History: find any answer and continue it
05-history-continue.why: Every question and answer is saved on this computer. Search, filter by mode, copy, or press Continue to keep going.
steps: Open 🕘 History
Search and expand an answer
Press Continue: the whole thread reopens
Ask a follow-up in that conversation

06-not-useful.title: Nothing to answer? “Not useful”
06-not-useful.why: If the screenshot has no question, code or error, Beast says so in one line instead of guessing.
steps: The screen is just a desktop wallpaper
Press ⌘↵
One line: ⚠️ Not useful — attach one that shows the question

07-debug.title: Debug mode (Claude Code CLI)
07-debug.why: Debug answers come from Claude Opus through your logged-in Claude Code CLI, for the best quality.
steps: Choose Debug
A stack trace is on the screen
Press ⌘↵
Root cause · evidence · fix · before vs after · verify

08-design-mcq-language.title: Design rounds, multiple choice, any language
08-design-mcq-language.why: The same screenshot flow handles system design prompts, MCQs (correct option + why) and questions in Hindi or other languages.
steps: Design: “Design a URL shortener” → full design answer
Concept: an MCQ → the right option + one line why
A question in Hindi → answer in Hindi

09-solve-screen.title: Solve screen: ⌘⇧O watches and answers new questions
09-solve-screen.why: Turn it on and Beast checks the screen every few seconds. Each new question is answered once, in the right mode.
steps: Press ⌘⇧O (or the Solve screen button)
An MCQ appears → found and answered
The screen changes to a coding problem → found too
The same question is never answered twice
Press ⌘⇧O again to stop

10-documents.title: Documents: résumé, notes, PDFs, logs
10-documents.why: Attach files with 📎 (or drag and drop). Beast reads them and answers using them.
steps: Click 📎 and pick a résumé PDF and notes
They wait in the tray, each can get a note
Ask: “Tell me about yourself”
The answer uses your own résumé

11-listen.title: Listen + live transcript
11-listen.why: Listen hears the meeting and your mic, and answers questions as soon as they are asked. Here the questions are played from the laptop speaker into its own mic (the desktop app reads meeting audio directly).
steps: Click 🎧 Listen (or ⌘⇧M): “Listening…”
The interviewer asks a question (spoken from the speakers)
Beast hears it and the answer opens by itself
Stop with ⌘⇧M · open 💬 Live transcript, turn on the mic
Each line: time · who spoke · text · auto-answer

12-shortcuts-stop.title: Shortcuts panel: test every shortcut, hide or quit
12-shortcuts-stop.why: The ⌨️ button lists every shortcut with what it does. Press one to see a green ✓, or use Try.
steps: Open ⌨️ Shortcuts & controls
Press shortcuts: each row gets a ✓ and the time
Try runs one, same as the keys
Stop Beast: Hide (⌘\) or Quit (asks first)
Terminal commands, click to copy
